chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Hammad ibn Udayis, from Imran ibn Humaran, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Should I shorten the prayer in the Sacred Mosque (Mecca) or complete it?' He said: 'If you shorten it, that is acceptable; and if you complete it, that is better, and the increase in goodness is goodness.'

key_terms.وَزِيَادَةُ الْخَيْرِ خَيْرٌ: And the increase in goodness is goodness

ai.seo_question: Should I shorten or complete my prayer when visiting Mecca?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfahani, Imam al-Hassan (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling for praying in Masjid al-Haram, affirming that while shortening the four-rak'ah prayer is valid (permissible), completing it is superior (mustahabb). This reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that the Sacred Mosque is a place of full prayer, distinguishing it from other locations where shortening is obligatory for travelers, thereby emphasizing the spiritual merit of offering complete worship in the holiest site.
